methodology_notes.split_basis: ALL figures (price, shares, EPS, historical FY-end prices used in the sanity check) are on the CURRENT post-10:1-forward-split basis. The split took effect 2025-11-17 (record date 2025-11-10, split-adjusted trading from 2025-11-17). NFLX_Metrics.csv is already split-adjusted throughout; no further conversion applied.
methodology_notes.wbd_fee_normalization: Q1-2026 'Interest and other income' includes a $2,800M cash termination fee from Paramount Skydance (paid on Warner Bros. Discovery's behalf after WBD's board deemed Paramount's competing bid superior, terminating its merger agreement with Netflix). This inflated Q1-2026 net income to $5,282.8M (43.1% margin) and Q1-2026 FCF to $5,094.1M. Q2-2026 FCF ($1,525.2M) was in turn depressed by cash taxes paid on that fee. FY2026 company FCF guidance of ~$12.5B INCLUDES the $2.8B fee; the analyst-normalized underlying FY2026 organic FCF is ~$10.2B (per guidance commentary), which is the figure used to sanity-check (not directly build) the Year-1 projection. The DCF's actual base year is FY2025 (a clean year, no WBD fee), with Year-1 (FY2026) built from components and cross-checked against this ~$10.2B normalized figure -- see 'fy2026_normalized_check' below.
methodology_notes.interest_income_treatment: Netflix does NOT disclose a clean 'interest income' line -- only a combined 'Interest and other income (expense)' that mixes FX gains/losses, derivative marks, and one-offs (this is the line the $2.8B WBD fee landed in: FY2023 -$48.8M, FY2024 +$266.8M, FY2025 +$172.5M). Per the mandatory rule, interest income is only stripped from owner FCF when net cash is material relative to the FCF base (to avoid double-counting a cash pile added back in EV). Netflix is NET DEBT (~$5.2B at Q2-2026: $14,309.3M total debt vs $9,099.2M cash), not net cash, so that double-count risk does not apply here. This combined line is therefore LEFT IN reported FCF/NI and not separately deducted in the owner-FCF build; the only deduction made is stock-based compensation (incl. cash taxes on equity awards).
methodology_notes.horizon: 5-year explicit projection. Owner-FCF margin matures from ~19.1% (Year 1, anchored to the WBD-fee-normalized FY2026 guidance) to ~24.0% (base case Year 5) -- a genuine but not still-steeply-ramping improvement, consistent with a 5-year horizon per the DCF skill's test (terminal-year margin roughly flat, not still climbing sharply).
methodology_notes.component_build_approach: Netflix's accounting makes a standard EBITDA->SBC->D&A->tax->capex->WC bridge misleading: content amortization (FY2025 $16,422.2M) runs through cost of revenue as an operating expense (already inside GAAP operating margin), while cash content SPEND is the real capital outlay embedded in operating cash flow, not capex. A reconciliation of FY2025 (NOPAT at the FY2025 effective cash tax rate of 16.66%, $11,106.2M, i.e. 24.58% of revenue) against actual reported FCF ($9,461.1M, 20.94% of revenue) shows a -3.64%-of-revenue residual -- this is the net effect of cash content spend running ahead of amortization plus other net working-capital movements (ex-deferred-revenue). The projections therefore use a single blended 'owner-FCF-margin' path per year, whose components (operating-margin guidance, cash-tax normalization, the content-spend-vs-amortization drag, and a deferred-revenue-style tailwind captured as ~15-20% of the YoY revenue increase) are documented narratively in 'assumptions' rather than run through a misleading generic bridge. Year-1 is anchored to the WBD-fee-normalized FY2026 guidance point (~19.1% margin) specifically so the model does not silently inherit an unrepeatable FY2025 windfall or ignore management's own guidance of margin pressure from front-loaded H1-2026 content amortization.

inputs.interest_income_note: NOT stripped -- see methodology_notes.interest_income_treatment. Netflix is a net-debt company; the combined interest/FX/other line is left inside reported FCF.
inputs.sbc_source: NFLX.duckdb kpis table (EquityAwardTaxes) + NFLX_Metrics.csv (StockBasedComp), both sourced from 10-K/10-Q cash flow statements and equity award footnotes
inputs.annual_share_growth_pct_note: Negative = net share count SHRINKS. Netflix buybacks ($9,127M FY2025, record $4,714M in Q2-2026 alone) far exceed SBC issuance, so uncovered dilution is zero and the share count declines. -2.0%/yr (base case) is deliberately conservative vs. the FY2023-2025 realized pace (avg shares declined ~1.8-2.7%/yr) and well below the Q2-2026 annualized pace, which is treated as a temporary peak funded partly by the one-off WBD fee proceeds.

fy2026_normalized_check.note: This is the guidance-based sanity anchor for Year 1 of the base case, NOT the number the projection is built from directly. The base-case Year-1 owner-FCF margin (19.1%) lands within 0.1pp of this, confirming the component build is not silently carrying forward an unrepeatable FY2025-level margin.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (5yr 19.2%, 3yr 8.6%) diverges materially from revenue CAGR (~12.6%) in BOTH directions across periods -- the 5yr figure is inflated by the low FY2020 equity base pre-buyback-era, and the 3yr figure is suppressed by $9.1B+ FY2025 buybacks shrinking the equity base even as earnings grew. Equity CAGR is therefore NOT used as the growth driver for this ticker; revenue CAGR is used per the ticker-specific instruction, since it is the only series clean of both the negative-FCF-year problem (FY2018-19, FY2021 owner FCF negative -- any FCF CAGR off that base is not meaningful) and the buyback-distortion problem (equity/BVPS).
historical_growth.notes: SBC-adjusted (owner) FCF only became consistently positive from FY2020 onward and was negative in FY2018, FY2019, and FY2021 (content-investment build years) -- a CAGR computed off any of those bases is mathematically undefined or meaningless, which is why revenue CAGR (~12.6%, converged across the 3yr and 5yr windows) is used as the sole growth driver, per the ticker-specific instruction. EPS CAGR (33-36%) is far above revenue CAGR, reflecting margin expansion plus buyback-driven share count reduction -- not representative of a sustainable forward growth rate and not used directly.

base.margin_path_rationale: Year 1 (FY2026) anchored to WBD-fee-normalized guidance (~19.1%, essentially flat vs FY2025's 20.02% actual, reflecting management's own flag of front-loaded H1-2026 content amortization pressuring near-term margins). Years 2-5 assume gradual, not steep, improvement: GAAP operating margin ramping from the 31.5% FY2026 guide toward the low-mid 30s (management targets continued expansion), cash tax rate normalizing from FY2025's unusually low 16.7% effective rate toward 21-23% (a drag on FCF, not a tailwind), and the content-spend-vs-amortization cash drag (calibrated to -3.64% of revenue in FY2025) narrowing gradually as content spend growth decelerates alongside revenue growth, partially offset by a revenue-growth-linked deferred-revenue tailwind (~17% capture rate on the YoY revenue increase, small in dollar terms for NFLX vs. e.g. DUOL because subscription deferred revenue is a modest ~$1.8B balance).

bull.narrative: Advertising inflection scales faster than guided ($3B FY2026 target beaten, live-sports/ad-tier execution strong), price increases stick with limited churn, AI production tooling (InterPositive) delivers real cost/time savings that widen margin faster than management's own targets, and the paused Paramount-WBD combination is blocked or materially delayed by the antitrust trial (mid-2027), pushing out the largest competitive threat.

bear.narrative: Growth deceleration confirmed in Q2/Q3-2026 continues (already the slowest since Q3-2023), price-increase fatigue and rotational/event-driven subscriber behavior pressure retention, reduced subscriber/engagement disclosure erodes investor confidence further, AI-native content tools erode the traditional studio production moat faster than Netflix's own AI tooling can offset, content cost inflation (sports rights, guild costs) outpaces revenue growth, and a reconstituted Paramount-WBD eventually closes and intensifies competition.

wacc_derivation.wacc_justification: The CAPM-derived WACC (10.52%, using beta 1.30, rf 4.3%, ERP 5.0%) sits at the upper end of the instructed 8.5-10% range. The base case uses 9.5% -- below the pure CAPM figure but above the range midpoint -- balancing two facts: (1) Netflix is a $315B+ investment-grade mega-cap with no small-cap/illiquidity premia warranted, arguing for the lower end; (2) the newly-prominent AI-content-disruption debate and two consecutive quarters of confirmed growth deceleration (16%->13%->11.7% guided) are real, elevated near-term risks not fully captured by a trailing beta, arguing for the upper end. 9.5% reflects that balance. Bull case uses 9.0% (risk resolving favorably), bear case uses 11.0% (risks materializing, consistent with the CAPM-derived figure plus a stress increment).

valuation.note: Gordon Growth binds (is lower than the 20x cap) in all three scenarios -- terminal value is not being artificially capped in the base/bull/bear central estimates. The cap only binds in the sensitivity matrix at low-WACC / high-terminal-growth corners (see sensitivity block), which is exactly the guardrail it is meant to provide.

entry_price.methodology: Entry = (sum of Yrs1-5 owner FCF discounted at 15%) + (Gordon terminal value, computed at WACC, discounted at 15%) - net_debt, all divided by the Year-5 projected share count. Interim FCF and net-debt adjustment are both included; only the terminal value's own math (not its discounting back to today) uses WACC.
entry_price.note: Base entry price ($45.27) sits well below base intrinsic value ($56.90) as expected -- base-case revenue growth decelerates from ~13% to ~7%, averaging below the 15% hurdle rate across the horizon, so the IRR-target price requires a meaningfully lower entry than fair value. Bull entry ($65.91) sits closer to bull IV ($84.94) since bull growth (9.5-14.5%) runs closer to the hurdle.

sensitivity.note: Base-case owner FCF path used for all cells; only WACC and terminal growth vary. Values at 75.00 (WACC 7.5%, all terminal growth points; WACC 8.5%, terminal growth 3.5-4.0%) are 20x-cap-bound -- Gordon growth would otherwise exceed the cap at those low-WACC/high-growth combinations.

sbc_noncash_memo.description: Memo value if SBC were treated as a purely non-cash accounting charge with zero economic cost to shareholders (i.e. owner FCF adjustment reversed, base-case growth/margin/WACC otherwise unchanged). The spread vs. the actual base IV is the honest measure of how much this valuation depends on SBC treatment.
sbc_noncash_memo.interpretation: The spread is small (~3.3% of IV) because NFLX's SBC is modest relative to revenue (0.92% of FY2025 revenue, well below high-SBC growth names) and shares are already shrinking net of SBC issuance via buybacks. SBC treatment is a minor driver of this valuation, unlike SBC-heavy non-repurchasing names.

sanity_check.methodology: Historical FY-end P/E (GAAP EPS), P/B, EV/EBITDA, and P/S computed FY2016-FY2025 using post-10:1-split-adjusted prices and CSV fundamentals. FY2016-2020 excluded from averages as hypergrowth-era outliers (P/E ran 78-288x during the pre-profitability-inflection years) but retained in the table per instruction. FY2021-onward is the relevant anchor era.
sanity_check.relevant_era_note: The FY2021-onward era (avg P/E ~41x, max ~54x) is the correct anchor -- a future reader should NOT 'correct' this by re-including the FY2016-2020 hypergrowth-era multiples (78-288x P/E), which reflect a pre-profitability-inflection market pricing subscriber growth rather than earnings.

trip_rules_checked.rule: upside > 100% AND price in upper half of 10yr range
trip_rules_checked.detail: Base-case upside is -23.25% (downside, not >100% upside); moot on price-position grounds too since current price ($74.14) is in the lower half of the 10yr range (down 41.5% from the 52-week high of $126.71).

trip_rules_checked.rule: implied exit multiple exceeds current trading multiple (assumes multiple expansion)
trip_rules_checked.detail: Base-case implied exit multiple (15.85x owner FCF) is well BELOW the current EV/reported-FCF multiple (33.9x) -- the model assumes significant multiple COMPRESSION from today's trading level by year 5, not expansion.

trip_rules_checked.rule: implied multiples at IV far exceed historical trading range (peak-earnings / overvaluation trip)
trip_rules_checked.detail: All implied multiples at base IV (P/E 22.5x, P/B 9.3x, EV/EBITDA 18.5x, P/S 5.5x) sit BELOW both the current-price multiples (P/E 29.3x, P/B 12.1x, EV/EBITDA 24.0x, P/S 7.1x) and the FY2021+ historical trading averages (P/E 41.2x, P/B 13.1x, EV/EBITDA 33.3x, P/S 7.8x). The model is conservative relative to how the market has actually priced NFLX post-hypergrowth, not aggressive.

sanity_check.verdict: PASS -- no trip rules fired, no auto-fix applied. The base-case DCF ($56.90, -23.25% vs current $74.14) sits below the market's current price, which itself already trades at a discount to its own FY2021+ average multiples following the 2026 selloff. This is an internally consistent, conservative result: the model does not require multiple expansion to reach fair value (implied exit multiple 15.85x is roughly half the current 33.9x EV/FCF), and the downside case reflects deceleration risk (revenue growth guided to 11.7% for Q3-2026, the slowest since Q3-2023) being modeled through rather than a broken assumption.

content_obligations_note: Netflix carries tens of billions of dollars in off-balance-sheet content obligations (multi-year licensing/production commitments), a large portion due within 12 months. These are NOT added to net_debt in this model -- they are operating commitments whose cash outflows are already reflected inside the projected owner-FCF path (via the content-spend-vs-amortization drag term and the underlying operating-margin assumptions). Adding them to net debt on top of deducting the associated cash spend from FCF would double-count the same economic obligation.
key_judgment_calls: Used revenue CAGR (~12.6%, converged 3yr/5yr) as the sole historical growth anchor, per ticker-specific instruction, since owner FCF was negative in 3 of the last 8 years (making any FCF CAGR meaningless) and equity CAGR is buyback-distorted in both directions across windows.

Did NOT strip the 'Interest and other income (expense)' line from owner FCF, despite it being where the $2.8B WBD fee landed, because Netflix is a net-debt (not net-cash) company and the double-count rationale for stripping interest income does not apply; instead, the WBD fee was normalized out at the guidance level (FY2026 $12.5B guide -> ~$10.2B normalized) purely as a sanity-check anchor for Year 1, not run through the historical owner-FCF series (FY2025, the DCF's actual base year, contains no WBD fee).

Replaced the standard EBITDA->capex bridge with a single blended owner-FCF-margin path per year (documented narratively) because content amortization sits inside GAAP operating income while cash content spend sits inside OCF, making a literal EBITDA-D&A-capex build double-count or miss the real capital outlay; the margin path is anchored empirically to the FY2025 NOPAT-vs-reported-FCF reconciliation (-3.64%-of-revenue drag) rather than assumed.

Set Year-1 (FY2026) owner-FCF margin to ~19.1%, essentially FLAT vs FY2025's 20.02% actual (not an improvement), specifically to avoid carrying forward FY2025's margin into a year guidance itself flags as pressured by front-loaded content amortization -- this is the single most consequential choice in the model and is what keeps the base case from overstating Year-1 cash generation.

WACC set at 9.5% (base), below the pure CAPM-derived 10.52% but above the range midpoint, balancing 'mega-cap, no small-cap premia' against 'AI-disruption + confirmed two-quarter growth deceleration' as a genuine near-term risk elevation -- not padded arbitrarily, but also not taken at the bottom of the stated 8.5-10% range given those live risks.

Share count projected to shrink at -2.0%/yr (base), deliberately conservative vs. the FY2023-2025 realized buyback pace and well below the Q2-2026 record $4.7B quarter (partly WBD-fee-funded and treated as a temporary peak, not a new run-rate).

No trip rules fired in the mandatory sanity check; no auto-fix (peak-earnings/WACC/growth/terminal-growth/exit-multiple-cap) was applied because the base-case implied multiples are conservative relative to both current trading multiples and the FY2021+ historical average.
